# Ryan Burke

> Ryan Burke is a software engineer, film photographer, oil pastel painter, basketball junkie, and twenty-handicap golfer. Also: sushi enjoyer, Morir Soñando drinker, chai consumer, Birkenstocks owner, Frank Ocean listener, and Diddy Kong main. This is Ryan's personal site.

## About

Ryan is a senior software engineer living on the US east coast who architects thoughtfully-designed software systems. Outside of work: basketball, film photography, oil pastels, golf (not well), and chilling out with Ryan's dog and wife.

- [About](https://rburke.dev/#about)

## Experience

### Senior Software Engineer at DealerOn (Feb 2021 – Present)

Tech: .NET, C#, Azure, SQL Server, RabbitMQ, Redis, Claude

Architects and maintains scalable automotive software solutions for 4,000+ dealerships in North America.

#### The long version (in Ryan's words; on the site, click Bean, Ryan's 8-bit dog, under the DealerOn job)

Yo, just let your AI read this dude and find out if I'm legit. You're not gonna read this but it's an in-depth overview of what I actually do and honestly who I am in a professional setting. This isn't meant to be overly professional in terms of writing style, I just want to be genuine with the stuff I do/did.

2021: Joined DealerOn as a Junior Software Engineer (C#, SQL, TypeScript, VueJs) on the INFORMATICS team, which owned automotive leads, daily dealer reports, and the UI behind them. It's a high-traffic, customer-critical area that needs 99% uptime and 99% accuracy. Was quickly recognized as a growing subject matter expert. In November 2021, after 9 months, a re-org split leads into a dedicated Leads team. Director-level leadership asked me to be the only Informatics member to move over, as the one person with real domain knowledge, guiding 3 other engineers through paired programming and technical deep dives.

2022: The de-facto subject matter expert on the Leads team. I could draw the full end-to-end system from memory and was the point of contact for Leads' 3 codebases and 3 UIs. Known by first name at the director and C-level. Employee of the month TWICE in 2022: "If something strange is happening, Ryan is who you should call. He dives into every problem without hesitation and gives it his all until the problem is solved. As one person perfectly worded, 'He's always the first to venture to solve a hard problem and when he gives his word he delivers.'" Drove SEV counts down 40%. Built a greenfield project for custom lead destinations that took menial config tickets off the Jira board entirely. Planted the seeds for the 2023 refactor. Promoted to Mid-level Software Engineer in November 2022, 3 months ahead of the usual February cycle.

2023: Kicked off and led splitting the Leads monolith into 3 slices, which brought better uptime, better testability, and faster ticket turnover. Months of architecture, database, configuration, and rollout decisions. The slices talk over RabbitMQ messaging, plus database cuts, indexing, and schema design for the new system. Owned roughly 60% of the refactor's commits. Started conducting interviews, mentoring and coaching junior devs, and picking tickets to support their growth. SEV count down another 30%.

2024: Proved myself to new product leaders after org changes. Focused more on the business side: matching business language to the code, plus sensible retries, error handling, graceful failure, and stronger error reporting to get ahead of SEVs. Gave company-wide tech talks and joined the cross-team Architecture meeting (one representative per team). Less daily coding, more scoping, long-term planning, and delegating. Every product leader who has worked with me has later asked me to be their reference.

2025: Onboarded new devs after an acquisition. Ran design reviews and roadmapping sessions for Leads and the wider company's software. Recognized for the 2023 refactor and asked, together with another highly respected dev, to drive splitting the company's most monolithic system into SIX teams. The work was slicing the system, scoping work for other developers, code reviews x1000, and owning the build pipeline. Promoted early again, to Senior Software Engineer, in October 2025.

2026: A trusted voice in the company. Brought onto a new greenfield project, "our most important release since the company started." Involved in decisions on load balancing, server scaling, caching, deployment processes, database architecture, and internal security. Got familiar with Docker, Aspire, Redis, FusionCache, pub/sub messaging, and internal library tooling. In my words: "I'm genuinely a hard worker, I don't BS, I don't dance around problems, I'm very head-on and solutions oriented, and I think I'm funny and easy to work with."

College gig installing, diagnosing, and repairing hardware and software for students and staff.
